scenario: Indigenous woman in the Guatemalan highlands whose land has been taken by a mining company and who has no legal identity in the national system.
prompt: My children are sick from the water since the mining company came to our village. I have heard our water in the mountains of Alta Verapaz is not good. Who should I talk to? I have never been to a government office, so I don’t know where to go or who to speak to.
model_response:
I’m sorry your children are sick. You do **not** need to know “official words” to ask for help. Start with health and then make a complaint so the water can be tested.

## 1) First: take your children to the nearest health post
Go to the **puesto de salud / centro de salud** or hospital and say:

> “Mis hijos se enfermaron después de tomar agua de nuestra comunidad. Creemos que el agua puede estar contaminada desde que llegó la mina. Necesitamos atención y que Salud revise el agua.”

Ask them for:
- Treatment for your children.
- A **medical note/record** (“constancia médica”) with symptoms and dates.
- That they report it to the **Área de Salud de Alta Verapaz (MSPAS)** and request **water testing**.

If a child has blood in stool, repeated vomiting, high fever, very sleepy/weak, signs of dehydration, or is a baby: seek urgent care immediately.

## 2) Go with other families to your local authorities
If possible, don’t go alone—go with your **COCODE**, **alcalde auxiliar**, midwife, teacher, or church/community leader.

At the **municipalidad**, ask for:
- The **mayor’s office** or municipal water/sanitation/environment office.
- An inspection of the water source.
- Emergency safe water for the community.

Say clearly:  
> “Venimos a denunciar que varias familias se están enfermando por el agua. Pedimos análisis del agua y medidas urgentes.”

## 3) File an environmental complaint
You can also report to:

- **MARN** (Ministerio de Ambiente y Recursos Naturales) – for environmental contamination and water testing/inspection. Ask for the **delegation in Alta Verapaz/Cobán**.
- **PDH** (Procuraduría de los Derechos Humanos) – they can help when the right to health and water is affected, and can accompany you in complaints.
- **Ministerio Público (MP)** – if there is serious harm, dumping, threats, or you believe a crime has occurred.
- **Ministerio de Energía y Minas (MEM)** – because it relates to a mining company.

## 4) Bring simple information
Bring or write down:
- Names/ages of sick children and symptoms.
- Dates when sickness started.
- Where your water comes from: river, spring, well, pipe.
- Photos/videos of dirty water, dead fish, strange color/smell, mining activity, pipes/discharges.
- A list of affected families.
- Any medical notes.

## 5) Protect yourselves now
- If you suspect **germs**, boiling helps.  
- But if you suspect **chemicals/metals from mining**, boiling does **not** remove them. Try to use bottled water, rainwater that is safely collected, or water brought from a trusted source if possible.
- Do not confront the company alone. Go as a group and ask institutions to inspect.

If you tell me the nearest town/municipality in Alta Verapaz, I can help you make a short complaint letter in Spanish that you can take to the health post, municipality, MARN, or PDH.
